objectives.description: Identify self, another person and a familiar referent; answer identity checks.
objectives.rationale: Personal, demonstrative and copular meanings support names, origin, occupation and face-to-face identification; P/F supply the open slot vocabulary.

objectives.description: Ask and answer person, thing, place, origin, time, quantity, reason and manner questions.
objectives.rationale: Close each question contrast with lexical interrogatives plus F quantity/time and P/H/T/W/C/S topic prerequisites; alternative choice uses o. Narrow bare price questions explicitly depend on ADV A1-F-297, not DET A1-D-081/A1-F-037: cuánto is invariable while cuesta/cuestan agrees with the priced subject. Retain F-297's scenario-specific A1 proposal versus the framework's broader A2 adverbial treatment; no claim of unrestricted amount/degree-question coverage.

objectives.description: Confirm, correct, contradict and seek a short confirmation.
objectives.rationale: Yes/no with appropriate scope and repetition suffice for basic correction; tag use requires a distinct discourse decision.

objectives.description: Describe a familiar person, object, place and immediate routine.
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite: P personal descriptions, H objects, T location, W study/work, C preferences and F copulas/quality/time. A1 short descriptions and present sequences are included; extended connected past narration is not claimed.

objectives.description: State a basic belief, ask a minimal opinion and express tentative knowledge.
objectives.rationale: Belief and no-knowledge constructions cover modest stance without adding each sentence as a lexical MWE; complex argument is outside A1.

objectives.description: Ask for and give a basic positive, negative or middling evaluation.
objectives.rationale: Satisfactory/unsatisfactory/so-so contrasts are covered; F adjectives and degree supply richer evaluations.

objectives.description: Add a matching positive or negative fact and make a short contrasting response.
objectives.rationale: F también/tampoco remain prerequisites alongside D yes/no and pero; shared-opinion MWE is separately proposed A2, not silently upgraded by a simple acknowledgment.

objectives.description: Express uncertainty or possibility without proving a conclusion.
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite: F A1-F-259 quizá/quizás and A1-F-260 ser posible, plus D creer. These original sense proposals need global form-versus-construction adjudication, not duplicate D rows.

objectives.description: Ask whether someone knows information, a person/place or a learned skill.
objectives.rationale: Keep factual saber, acquaintance conocer and F A1-F-261 learned-skill saber distinct; inability and ignorance are ordinary negated practice, not new words. F A1-F-261 learned-skill saber remains a prerequisite, not duplicated into another new D row.

objectives.description: State liking/disliking, a preference and a want; offer a simple choice.
objectives.rationale: Liking, preferring and wanting each need a meaning decision. Questions about interest are A2 in 3.1 but minimal offers and alternatives occur at A1; do not infer a universal minimum from one function.

objectives.description: Ask and state immediate plans using familiar activities and times.
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite: F present-tense/calendar/time system and P/H/T/W/C action senses; present with a future time is practice material. Pragmatics 2.5 locates a richer future-present treatment at A2; preserve this framework granularity rather than invent a new ir meaning.

objectives.description: Handle a brief well-being answer and signal an immediate physical need.
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite: P differentiated affect/body/health inventory and its explicit A1 emergency/need exceptions versus A2 thematic recommendations; bien/mal crosslinks here. No blanket early introduction of all feelings or all health words.

objectives.description: Understand short classroom requests and ask for slower/repeated speech.
objectives.rationale: Repetition, understanding and silence need lexical coverage. Prerequisite F A1-F-189 despacio, quantity más and W classroom actions; no separate word for every imperative or full request.

objectives.description: Request an object or immediate assistance and accept or refuse.
objectives.rationale: Object plus courtesy marker and yes/no response close A1; explicit urgent-help exception links T. Indirect favours and strategic evasion are later, not required to name every act.

objectives.description: Grant/deny permission and make a bounded classroom/service permission request.
objectives.rationale: Grant/refusal are A1 in the checked function columns; asking permission is A2 there. Propose only immediate permission as a visible A1 extension with an independent modal meaning, not a runtime change.

objectives.description: Offer a familiar item and accept or decline courteously.
objectives.rationale: Wanting, familiar object labels, yes/no and thanks suffice; detailed invitations and commitments remain later comparisons.

objectives.description: Greet and answer in morning, later daytime and night contexts.
objectives.rationale: Bound greetings by time/social function, not every possible person-name combination.

objectives.description: Attract attention and choose an appropriate address form.
objectives.rationale: Courtesy marker, brief interjection and F tú/usted are selected. Prerequisite P A1-P-165/166 señor/señora form-family adjudication; neither age nor nationality mechanically determines address.

objectives.description: Respond to meeting a person and exchange names.
objectives.rationale: A conventional pleasure formula differs from ordinary happiness; personal introductions depend on P names and F identity forms.

objectives.description: Apologize briefly, express sympathy and acknowledge an apology.
objectives.rationale: Apology, regret/sympathy and acknowledgment are distinct contrasts; source placements and any earlier extension are visible per selection.

objectives.description: Thank someone and acknowledge thanks.
objectives.rationale: All five planned social identities are reconciled; response formula has an explicit A1 proposal despite the function inventory's A2 column.

objectives.description: Use a brief congratulation and a toast without assuming a religious occasion.
objectives.rationale: Conventional celebratory meanings differ from health/happiness nouns; P/C/S provide occasion vocabulary without copying an exhaustive holiday list.

objectives.description: End a brief exchange and acknowledge the other speaker's departure.
objectives.rationale: General, tomorrow-bound and later-encounter farewells are covered; variable day slots belong to F calendar practice.

objectives.description: Signal attention, keep listening and request a person in a face-to-face exchange.
objectives.rationale: A greeting, an interested sí and name/title request suffice; telephone technology and conversational transfer are not equivalent lexical senses.

objectives.description: Connect additions, alternatives, contrasts, causes and an example.
objectives.rationale: Core connectors plus a lexical example marker close short discourse; rhetorical concessions and multi-point argument belong later.

objectives.description: Put two or three familiar actions into temporal order.
objectives.rationale: Reuse temporal antes/después and F ordinal/time prerequisites. Explicit rhetorical ordering is A2 in pragmatics; short A1 chronological practice is a bounded proposal, not proof all ordering markers are A1.

objectives.description: Signal non-understanding, request a word, repetition, spelling or changed delivery.
objectives.rationale: The three planning sentence seeds are compositional usage frames. W supplies palabra/frase/letra/deletrear; F supplies cómo/otra/quantity and slower pace; D keeps explicit speech-volume senses. Unresolved prerequisite: the bounded naming frame cómo se dice requires nonreflexive se analysis and an explicit early-use teaching decision. A1-F-030 covers reflexive/pronominal routines and does not supply this use. Its classroom-frame introduction, agreement with a named expression and any extension to productive impersonal/passive constructions must be adjudicated with F/W before learner authoring; lexical coverage does not discharge that grammar dependency.

objectives.description: Control person forms, polite force and region-sensitive choices.
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite F/P tú, usted, ustedes, vosotros and clitics plus W alphabet/letter-name paradigm. Compare es-ES default with valid regional forms including vos, without demanding productive mastery of every paradigm. T A1-T-101 coger needs a regional usage warning; native/audio checks remain later.

objectives.description: Distinguish a statement, yes/no question, information question, vocative and polite request.
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite physical playback QA and independent listening: lexical stress, vowel linking, meaningful pauses, polite versus curt delivery and question types. A rise is a useful default for some total questions, not a universal Spanish-question rule. Slovak fixed initial stress must not be transferred.

objectives.description: Spell names and give a number, date or time without minting every combination.
frameworkSections: Functions 1.2; W spelling objective; F number/time objectives
objectives.rationale: Prerequisite W Spanish 27-letter alphabet including ñ, ch/ll digraphs, recommended letter names plus valid regional ye/i griega and uve/ve-type variants; F bounded numeral and calendar paradigms. Letter spelling and verbal pronunciation are different skills.

objectives.description: Use eye contact, pointing, turn-yielding and a visible closing cue.
objectives.rationale: Applicable to course practice but not lexical-sense enumeration: nonverbal acts are explicitly accounted for and require later accessible multimodal practice, not fabricated word entries.

objectives.description: Reserve explicit viewpoint positioning, recall and elaborated feeling/attitude work for later comparison.
objectives.rationale: These checked A1 columns are blank or covered only by simpler functions. P/F own recall, obligation and feelings with exceptions; A2-D owns developed positioning and emotion exchanges. Later placement is a recommendation, not a ban on simple utterances containing the same senses.

objectives.description: Reserve developed favours, suggestions, advice, warning and offer-to-help routines.
objectives.rationale: Checked A1 columns are blank. A1 lexical help and a safety recognition prerequisite T do not claim coverage of all indirect requests, warning strategies, suggestions or advice; routine development belongs A2-D.

objectives.description: Reserve elaborate welcome/wishes and written social correspondence.
frameworkSections: Functions 5.8–5.9, 5.17–5.18; written A2 portions of 5.1 and 5.21
objectives.rationale: A1 greetings/thanks can participate in these events but do not require every welcome, wish, holiday formula or letter closing as a lexical selection. Later A2-D handles the finite conventional families.

objectives.description: Reserve telephone routing, message-taking and extended story management.
objectives.rationale: C/T own devices, messages and accommodation, while A2-D supplies transfers, call errors, story openings and interruptions. A1 lexical repair is retained; richer discourse-function occurrence does not force its base words later.

objectives.description: Account for explicitly unpopulated A1/A2 functional headings.
objectives.rationale: These framework placeholders are not missing Wordfold word lists. No invented quota or claim that a placeholder prohibits incidental communication; later inventories must inspect their own populated headings.

selections.sense: say words or convey information aloud
selections.levelRationale: Naming a word and asking how it is said require the speech meaning.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: The planning seed cómo se dice is a construction of this verb, not a separate lexical word.
selections.register: neutral; contextual politeness and turn function matter
selections.region: pan-Hispanic meaning; es-ES default audio with regional variation respected
selections.formNotes: Digo/dices/dice. The proposed classroom naming frame uses nonreflexive se, not the reflexive/pronominal se in A1-F-030. Distinguish impersonal third-singular analysis from passive-reflexive analysis with patient-subject agreement; a quoted or singular expression does not by itself establish one analysis for every open slot. Bound initial practice to one named expression, and require a later explicit agreement/generality decision rather than teach invariant dice for every plural subject. No new verb or sentence-word for each form.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Check c before i under the selected es-ES voice, final r in infinitive and clear stress in dice. Unstressed se links to dice; tonic cómo carries question prominence, without making se reflexive or treating every information question as rising.
uncertainties: Global ownership and sense boundary must be adjudicated with F/P and the relevant topical cell; this row is not an additional published word.

The classroom naming frame is an explicit bounded A1 proposal, not covered by reflexive A1-F-030. PCIC grammar 7.1.4 A1 supplies reflexive se, while RAE DPD se distinguishes impersonal and passive-reflexive syntax without assigning a learner level. Global adjudication must decide the frame's analysis, slot/agreement limits and introduction separately from unrestricted productive se grammar; this unresolved dependency blocks freeze.

exclusions.subject: Planning seed ¿Cómo se dice…? as a separate word
exclusions.reason: Exclude a new full-sentence lexical entry, not the required classroom frame. Cómo plus nonreflexive se plus decir and one named-expression slot is proposed as bounded A1 practice. F supplies the interrogative, but A1-F-030 explicitly covers only reflexive/pronominal se and cannot satisfy this construction. RAE DPD se 2.1–2.2 distinguishes impersonal syntax from passive-reflexive subject agreement; checked PCIC grammar 7.1.4 gives no A1 nonreflexive-se coverage here. An explicit F/W/D dependency must settle early frame introduction, grammatical analysis and plural-slot agreement before learner authoring; unrestricted impersonal/passive grammar is not thereby introduced. W supplies palabra/language names. Direct and polite question prosody remains later authoring work.

exclusions.subject: Planning seed ¿Puede repetir? and its tú/usted/plural variants as separate words
exclusions.reason: Exclude sentence/per-person duplication. Existing poder and repetir plus F agreement supply the bounded polite repetition request. Compare puede/puedes and address explicitly; optional object and por favor are practice, not extra senses.

exclusions.subject: Planning seed no entiendo and affirmative/negative understanding frames as separate words
exclusions.reason: Exclude compositional negation plus entender inflection. Practice must contrast genuine non-understanding, request for a slower delivery and uncertainty about facts, with intelligible not accusatory prosody.

exclusions.subject: Every information-question and answer sentence
exclusions.reason: Do not mint dónde + estar, cómo + llamarse, cuánto + costar, noun-plus-o choice, de dónde origin, por qué reason, para + infinitive purpose or a + destination as whole lexical MWEs. Their lexical prerequisites and constructions are explicitly covered; isolated native-like sounding sentences are not a sense count.

exclusions.subject: Every short opinion/confirmation/offer/refusal formula
exclusions.reason: Creer + que, no + saber, yo + también/tampoco, sí + pero, querer + item, item + por favor, sí/no + gracias and no + lo siento are productive practice frames. Keep selected lexical components and the genuinely conventional social formulas, not every combination as a word.

exclusions.subject: Every permission question and every imperative form
exclusions.reason: Poder permission is an explicit proposed meaning; ¿Puedo + infinitive? is not an extra MWE. W basic instructions use finite forms of selected actions. Do not duplicate tú/usted/ustedes/vosotros forms as senses or accidentally present permission as obligation.

exclusions.subject: All possible greetings, named vocatives and day-specific farewells
exclusions.reason: Select bounded conventional families; do not enumerate every person name, honorific combination or hasta + weekday/date as a new lexical sense. F calendar and P address forms provide productive slots. Named-person and greeting/time-formula granularity remains adjudication work.

exclusions.subject: Shushing sound spelling as an ordinary word
exclusions.reason: A1 quiet-request practice may include nonlexical shushing, but competing sh/ss/ch transcriptions are not new Spanish lexical senses. Select silencio and require intelligible multimodal/audio practice rather than counting a sound effect.

exclusions.subject: Advanced argument, concession, irony and idiom repertoire
exclusions.reason: Screened later supplemental argument/stance/discourse entries; their meanings are not required to close this A1 cell. Existing B1 opinar, aunque, por si acaso and later B2–C2 argument markers remain later-cell responsibilities, not excluded from the complete course. The shared-opinion estar de acuerdo collision is explicitly recorded here.

exclusions.subject: Unbounded courtesy alternatives and every regional acknowledgment
exclusions.reason: No attempt to inventory all regional equivalents of vale or all welcome, wish and letter-closing formulas at A1. Neutral yes/thanks/greeting choices remain available; A2-D must explicitly adjudicate welcome, wish, apology response and more developed conversational families.

exclusions.subject: Coger taboo meaning as an A1 learning target
exclusions.reason: The vulgar sexual meaning is not selected here. Prerequisite T A1-T-101 transport coger retains its ordinary Spain use, with a source-checked warning that another meaning is vulgar in named American regions. Offer context-appropriate tomar for travel; never claim all American speakers or every coger utterance are taboo.

exclusions.subject: Specialist health or emotional taxonomy from a repair/help need
exclusions.reason: A request for urgent help does not justify automatically promoting every body part, psychological state or clinical term. P/T explicitly own immediate need and emergency exceptions; their same-sense early/later decisions stay unresolved at global adjudication.

D has zero primary legacy category ownership. All 685 baseline identities were screened at term/meaning level for D relevance; all 81 A1 supplemental definitions were reread. This manifest directly adjudicates 30 relevant A1 expansion identities, 25 legacy identities and one B1 expansion identity, including the health-noun contrast linked to social salud. Other topical meanings remain in their primary cells, not duplicated to inflate D counts.

Of the 81 A1 expansions, unlinked lexical prerequisites are explicit: 003 possession, 004 existence, 005/010 motion, 006 activity, 011 visual perception, 014 placement, 015–018 calendar units, 021 yesterday, 025–035 numerals, 036–041 colors, 042–060 weekdays/months, 079 possession de, 080 static en and 081 definite el belong to F and topic-slot practice. They are not missing greetings/discourse senses; their exact baseline identities stay in F/P/H/T/W/C/S manifests.

Exactly five A1 social planned identities are directly selected here, with P A1-P-277–281 treated as crosslinks to these same proposals. Five A1 function-word planned identities are direct D cross-references. The identity, listening/looking/bringing/searching/drinking, time and quantity planned families are F/P/W/H/T/C prerequisites, not new D outcomes or silent deletions.

Cross-cell prerequisite closure: F A1-F-253 complementizer que, -257 también, -258 tampoco, -259 quizá/quizás, -260 ser posible, -261 learned-skill saber, -189 despacio, -205 regular and -136 momento. P names/address/people/body/health supply introduction and need slots. H meal-order pedir and object nouns, T urgent socorro and travel coger, W classroom words/spelling, and C phone/media/activity meanings remain primary-cell lexical responsibilities.

All six functional sections are mapped through objectives, including unpopulated placeholders, later A2 comparisons and applicable nonlexical/nonverbal practice. No blanket claim that every function requires a new word or that a later thematic occurrence fixes minimum introduction. No deferred-core objective is used to disguise missing A1 lexical contrasts.

Formula granularity remains open: fixed social formulas versus productive clauses, timed greetings as a family, INTJ analysis for lo siento/qué tal, ADJ introduction encantado, no confirmation tag versus negation, and permission poder versus ability. Counts are rows only; shared references and synonyms are not automatically net additions.

Sequence boundary: temporal before/after and F ordinal/time dependencies allow two or three familiar chronological steps. PCIC pragmatic rhetorical ordering is A2; longer narrative ordering, por último and extended story management remain A2-D decisions rather than extra A1 words.

Register/pronunciation closure is a prerequisite, not an attestation: es-ES default playback must cover tú/usted contrasts, valid regional pronouns and letter names, question versus statement versus vocative contours, linked formula rhythm, word stress and courteous/abrupt force. Regional vale/coger notes need native editorial review. No statement that all Spanish questions rise, all Latin America uses one form, or Slovak spelling predicts Spanish stress.

Finite closure test for later adjudication: demonstrate openings/replies, identification and each question contrast, belief/evaluation and matching/opposing response, want/like/prefer, immediate needs/requests and permission, offers/acceptance/refusal, apology/sympathy/thanks/replies, congratulations/toast/farewell, attention/backchannel, addition/alternative/contrast/reason/example, brief chronological sequence and repair of word/repetition/pace/volume/spelling. New synonyms are admitted only for a missing sense/register/region contrast, not an arbitrary quota.

Controller correction: bare price-question coverage is a prerequisite crosslink to ADV A1-F-297, distinct from DET A1-D-081/A1-F-037. Retain the shared planned ID and the unresolved narrow-A1/general-A2 introduction distinction; no new D row is counted.

Controller correction: excluding the whole classroom naming question as a word does not remove its required nonreflexive-se construction. A1-F-030 does not cover it. D repair and decir now record the unresolved F/W/D introduction, impersonal-versus-passive analysis, expression-slot and agreement dependency with checked PCIC grammar and RAE DPD evidence. This is a bounded frame proposal, not proof that productive impersonal/passive se is an A1 prerequisite already delivered.

Remaining uncertainty is deliberate and blocks global freeze: cell acceptance approves enumeration work only; placements, grammar dependencies and shared-sense ownership still need cross-level adjudication and independent language review.
